paper.title: UrbanVR: An immersive analytics system for context-aware urban design

relevant_section_or_figure: Section 4.4, Viewpoint Optimization; Figures 5-6. The authors formalize a target view with an energy function combining target-distance fit (E1), camera obstruction avoidance (E2), and target view-occlusion minimization (E3); Figure 6 contrasts the individual terms with their combined result.
transferable_principle: In a spatial visualization, treat legibility as a view-construction problem: define semantic targets and occluders using cheap spatial abstractions, then optimize the camera (or presentation layer) for a bounded target distance, unobstructed placement, and minimal target occlusion while preserving context. Do not rely on a static camera or global translucency to solve clutter.
application_to_world_v21: For the currently selected task parcel, receipt, worker trace, or epistemic-state cluster, build a lightweight proxy set from the live snapshot/SSE scene and score candidate camera poses against (1) target scale in the viewport, (2) camera-inside-geometry safety, and (3) occlusion by terrain/geometry/other parcels. Keep the rest of the world as context, but use semantic LOD proxies and an anchored state panel/label for the target. Recompute the framing when selection or EON time changes; this directly addresses pale terrain, weak scale, clutter, and unreadable state without copying UrbanVR's appearance.
falsifier: Reject this principle if a controlled A/B test on the same World v21 identification task shows that optimized framing does not improve target-state identification time, target readability, or measured occlusion rate over the baseline camera, or if users consistently prefer manual navigation after equivalent practice.
fake_evidence: None. The paper citation, section/figure references, and study claim are taken from the primary arXiv manuscript and its linked journal record; no World v21 result is presented as already observed.
